extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, physicists, and advanced students studying classical mechanics, gravitation, and geometric optics (readers of Newton's Principia)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and records propositions, corollaries, and methodological statements from a Latin treatise on attraction, motion in resisting media, and geometrical optics; useful for readers reproducing or applying Newtonian proofs and constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cylinder attraction (Corol. 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unde si solidum Cylindrus sit, parallelogrammo ADEB circa axem AB revoluto descriptus, & vires centripetæ in singula ejus puncta tendentes sint reciproce ut quadrata distantiarum a punctis: erit attractio corpusculi P in hunc Cylindrum ut BA - PE + PD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivation uses ordinatim applicata FK and areas: contributions from strips parallel to axis produce areas proportional to inverse-square distances; subtracting parts yields resultant area LABI equal to 1 in AB - PE + PD, hence force proportional to AB - PE + PD. (Explains how to reduce 3D integration to area computations for cylinders.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Spheroid attraction ratio (Corol. 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hinc etiam vis innotescit qua Sphærois AGBCD attrahit corpus quodvis P, exterius in axe suo AB situm. ... Vis qua Sphærois trahit corpus P erit ad vim qua Sphæra, diametro AB descripta, trahit idem corpus, ut (AS × CSq. - PS × KMRK) / (PSq. + CSq. - ASq.) ad AS cub.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a formula relating the attraction of a spheroid to that of a sphere of diameter AB via geometric quantities (AS, CS, PS, and a conic-section segment KMRK). Indicates the same computational foundation yields the forces of spheroidal segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attraction inside spheroid proportional to distance (Corol. 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quod si corpusculum intra Sphæroidem in data quavis ejusdem diametro collocetur; attractio erit ut ipsius distantia a centro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses pairs of concentric spheroids and cancels equal conical and segment contributions; shows net attraction comes only from the innermost spheroid and is proportional to distance PS to center AS, reproducing the internal linear law (harmonic/Hooke-like) for spheroids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverse problem: find decrement law of centripetal forces (Prop. XCII Prob. XLVI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dato corpore attractivo, invenire rationem decrementi virium centripetarum in ejus puncta singula tendentium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given a attracting body, one can form a sphere or cylinder (or other regular figure) whose attraction-law matches any given local decrement law (per Propositions LXXX–XCI). Then perform experiments measuring attraction at various distances to reveal the global law and thereby determine the decrement ratio of the partwise forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attraction of half-infinite body with particle-law exponent n (Prop. XCIII Theor. XLVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si solidum ex una parte planum, ex reliquis autem partibus infinitum, constet ex particulis æqualibus æqualiter attractivis, quarum vires in recessu a solido decrescunt in ratione potestatis cujusvis distantiarum plusquam quadraticæ, & vi solidi totius corpusculum ad utramvis plani partem constitutum trahatur: dico quod solidi vis illa attractiva, in recessu ab ejus superficie plana, decrescet in ratione potestatis, cujus latus est distantia corpusculi a plano, & Index ternario minor quam Index potestatis distantiarum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed proof splits the solid into parallel planes and reduces the total attraction to an area integral whose asymptotics give decay like distance^{-(n-3)} where n is exponent of particle attraction. Two cases handled: particle outside near the plane (Case 1) and particle placed inside (Case 2); corollaries show how distant parts can be neglected and state limits of the assertion (fails for particle-law exponent 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollaries about half-infinite solid (Corol. 1–3 of Prop. XCIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corol.1: If solid is bounded by two parallel infinite planes, its attraction can be obtained by subtracting attraction of the further infinite part. Corol.2: Distant parts' attraction becomes negligible and decreases approximately as CG^{n-3}. Corol.3: For finite bodies with one planar side made of homogeneous particles with particle-law exponent >4, the total attraction decays approximately as the small distance raised to index n-3; fails for exponent 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives practical asymptotic rules for neglecting remote mass and for how overall attraction scales with proximity to a planar face; warns the exception when particle-law exponent equals 3 (logarithmic/infinite contributions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholium on motion under planar attraction and series expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: If a body is attracted perpendicularly to a given plane under a specified attraction-law, the motion can be solved by reducing to the one-dimensional descent problem and by composing that motion with uniform motion parallel to the plane; operations are often performed by expanding ordinatim applicata in convergent series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the method of resolving applied ordinates into series expansions (binomial expansion) to obtain forces and resulting trajectories; examples: if ordinatim applied is parabola (m=2,n=1) gives Galileo's parabola result; if hyperbola (m=-1,n=1) leads to hyperbolic trajectory. Emphasizes using series to approximate and integrate contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refraction/reflection law from successive parallel media (Prop. XCIV Theor. XLVIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si media duo similaria, spatio planis parallelis utrinq; terminato, distinguantur ab invicem, & corpus in transitu per hoc spatium attrahatur vel impellatur perpendiculariter versus medium alterutrum, ... dico quod sinus incidentiæ in planum alterutrum erit ad sinum emergentiæ ex plano altero in ratione data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates that for a body traversing successive thin parallel layers with given perpendicular impulses, the sine of incidence on the next plane is to sine of emergence from the previous plane in a fixed ratio; proof uses limiting process with parabolic arcs and area/square relations. This is a mechanical derivation of Snell-like sine laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Velocity ratio equals sine ratio (Prop. XCV Theor. XLIX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Iisdem positis; dico quod velocitas corporis ante incidentiam est ad ejus velocitatem post emergentiam, ut sinus emergentiæ ad sinum incidentiæ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By decomposing motion into perpendicular and parallel components, and noting attraction/impulse acts only on perpendicular part, the time intervals give proportional path lengths; hence tangents (velocities) are in ratio of sines of emergent and incident angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflection with equal angles when emergent slower than incident (Prop. XCVI Theor. L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Iisdem positis & quod motus ante incidentiam velocior sit quam postea: dico quod corpus, inclinando lineam incidentiæ, reflectetur tandem, & angulus reflexionis fiet æqualis angulo incidentiæ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows that for successive thin-layered influences, if the emergent condition makes sine emergent equal to a radius (i.e., critical condition), the path becomes tangent and the body cannot pass beyond, reversing and emerging with equal angle; limiting process yields equality of incident and reflected angles (mechanical analogue of reflection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholium on analogy with light (optical remark)
rubrics_metrics.description: Harum attractionum haud multum dissimiles sunt Lucis reflexiones & refractiones, factæ secundum datam Secantium rationem, ut invenit Snellius, & per consequens secundum datam Sinuum rationem, ut exposuit Cartesius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observes that trajectories of bodies under these centripetal impulse laws mirror ray paths of light; suggests refraction is produced by gradual curvature rather than instantaneous change, and notes dispersion (different refrangibility) limits perfect optical correction by simple spherical figures; recommends using elliptic/hyperbolic surfaces for improved off-axis performance and combining elements (e.g., water between glass) to correct errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface-finding for focusing (Prop. XCVII Prob. XLVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Posito quod sinus incidentiæ in superficiem aliquam sit ad sinum emergentiæ in data ratione, quodq; incurvatio viæ corporum juxta superficiem illam fiat in spatio brevissimo, determinare superficiem quæ corpuscula omnia de loco dato successive manantia convergere faciat ad alium locum datum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: for given A (source) and B (target), and given ratio of sines, take a point C on axis AB and use increments CM and CN in prescribed ratio; with centers A and B describe circles intersecting at D; the tangent at D determines the desired curve CDE. Corollaries recover Cartesian refraction surfaces when endpoints at infinity. This is a geometric construction for refracting surfaces that send all rays from A to B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollaries on focusing surfaces (Corol. 1–2 of Prop. XCVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corol.1: Letting A or B go to infinity recovers the refraction figures given by Descartes. Corol.2: If rays incident and emergent are straight lines at given angles, increments PD and QD are generated so that PD:QD are sines incident:emergent, and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows how the construction generalizes to classical optical cases and gives the converse property: specifying geometric increments yields the sine ratio relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface synthesis: secondary attracting surface to re-converge rays (Prop. XCVIII Prob. XLVIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Iisdem positis, & circa axem AB descripta superficie quacunq; attractiva CD, regulari vel irregulari, per quam corpora de loco dato A exeuntia transire debent: invenire superficiem secundam attractivam EF, quæ corpora illa ad locum datum B convergere faciat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given a first refracting surface CD and desired focusing to B, extend AB to G with BG:CE = M-N:N (M,N given sine ratios), then construct auxiliary points H,K,L and draw tangent-construction centered at D to determine EF; proof composes the sine-ratio relations and shows EF will refract a ray through D to pass through B. Method extends to multiple surfaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholium on lens figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Eadem methodo pergere liceret ad superficies tres vel plures. Ad usus autem Opticos maxime accommodatæ sunt figuræ Sphæricæ. ... Talia vitra Objectiva vitris Ellipticis & Hyperbolicis præferenda sunt, ... Nisi corrigi possint errores illinc oriundi, labor omnis in cæteris corrigendis imperite collocabitur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: spherical surfaces are convenient but elliptic/hyperbolic surfaces correct off-axis rays better; compound lenses (e.g., two spherical faces with water between) can correct refraction errors; warns about chromatic dispersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resistance proportional to velocity: lost motion equals distance (Liber II Prop. I Theor. I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporis, cui resistitur in ratione velocitatis, motus ex resistentia amissus est ut spatium movendo confectum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If resistance per time is proportional to velocity (i.e., retardation per instant ∝ v), then the motion lost in each time element equals the distance traversed in that element; integrating gives total lost motion proportional to total distance traveled. Corollary: if body moves in a medium with only that resistance, given initial total motion and remaining motion after some distance, the total attainable distance is proportional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma on continuous proportionality (Lemma I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitates differentiis suis proportionales, sunt continue proportionales. Sit A ad A - B ut B ad B - C & C ad C - D &c. & dividendo fiet A ad B ut B ad C & C ad D &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A technical lemma used to pass from discrete proportionality of successive differences to continuous proportionality as the partition is refined; foundational for continuum limits in later propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric progression of velocities under linear resistance (Prop. II Theor. II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si corpori resistitur in ratione velocitatis, & sola vi insita per Medium similare moveatur, sumantur autem tempora æqualia: velocitates in principiis singulorum temporum sunt in progressione Geometrica, & spatia singulis temporibus descripta sunt ut velocitates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dividing time into equal parts and assuming resistance impulses proportional to velocity yields that velocities at the start of each time interval form a geometric progression; distances traversed in each interval are proportional to those velocities. As the partition refines, the continuous-time limit holds. Corollary: relates hyperbolic-area constructions to time/space under this resistance law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion with gravity plus linear resistance (Prop. III Prob. I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporis, cui dum in Medio similari recta ascendit vel descendit, resistitur in ratione velocitatis, quodq; ab uniformi gravitate urgetur, definire motum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructs motion via hyperbola and area methods: decomposes into many small equal times, shows the velocities/increments are in geometric progression, and uses areas under hyperbola to express times and distances. Corollaries: (1) relation between maximal attainable velocity and velocity at a given time via gravity and resisting excess; (2) sums of velocities behave geometrically; (3) differences of spaces in equal times decrease geometrically; (4) space described equals difference of two terms proportional to time and to initial velocity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projectile with linear resistance (Prop. IV Prob. II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Posito quod vis gravitatis in Medio aliquo similari uniformis sit, ac tendat perpendiculariter ad planum Horizontis; definire motum Projectilis, in eodem resistentiam velocitati proportionalem patientis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a hyperbolic-area construction for the projectile path (curve DraF) when resistance ∝ velocity and gravity constant. Gives method to recover the trajectory, initial speed, and resistance law from experimental impact points: choose trial resistance ratio, compute theoretical endpoints DF, Df, compare to observed F,f, and iterate to find true resistance-to-gravity ratio via plotting differences; corollaries show how the limiting parabola arises when certain relations hold, and how to deduce resistance/velocity distributions along curve. Scholium notes the linear-resistance hypothesis is mathematical and approximative; in very rarefied media quadratic resistance may be more appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadratic resistance: velocities inverse-geometric and equal interval spaces (Prop. V Theor. III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si corpori resistitur in velocitatis ratione duplicata, & sola vi insita per Medium similare movetur, tempora vero sumantur in progressione Geometrica a minoribus terminis ad majores pergente: dico quod velocitates initio singulorum temporum sunt in eadem progressione Geometrica inverse, & quod spatia sunt æqualia quæ singulis temporibus describuntur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When resistance ∝ (velocity)^2, and time intervals are chosen in geometric progression, the initial velocities of those intervals form an inverse geometric progression, and the distances traversed in equal time intervals are equal. Corollaries: relate hyperbolic-area representations to spaces under quadratic resistance, provide a way to express resistance magnitude via tangent constructions, and give proportionality relations to gravity or any given centripetal force.
